newsitem.title: USA: Dow Chemical implant case ends in mistrial.
newsitem.headline: Dow Chemical implant case ends in mistrial.

text.p: Dow Chemical Co said a mistrial was declared on Wednesday in the first-ever class action silicone breast implant case being tried in a state court here.
Louisiana District Court Judge Yada Magee ended the trial on the grounds of "prejudicial misconduct" during court proceedings by plaintiff's counsel.
The misconduct included "gestures made by counsel and non-verbal communications made by counsel to jurors," Magee said in a court order declaring the mistrial.
The jury in the three-month long trial was not immediately dismissed so the judge's decision could be appealed, Magee said in a separate order.

The suit initially covered an estimated 14,000 women who received silicone breast implants manufactured by the now bankrupt Dow Corning Inc. The case was pared down to focus on damages claimed by eight class representatives, with the remainder of the case transferred to a Michigan federal court at the urging of Dow Chemical.

The Louisiana suit alleges Dow Chemical, owner of 50 percent of Dow Corning, was liable for health problems stemming from the implants because it allegedly tested silicone compounds in its laboratories for Dow Corning.
